triggers: a kernel on NVIDIA Blackwell GeForce/workstation (RTX PRO 5000 / SM120) risks the '5. Assuming smaller chunks mean more overlap and better performance' trap

payload.goal: Avoid a known trap on NVIDIA Blackwell GeForce/workstation (RTX PRO 5000 / SM120): 5. Assuming smaller chunks mean more overlap and better performance

problem.statement: SM120 RMSNorm-MLP PDL Pitfalls -- 5. Assuming smaller chunks mean more overlap and better performance

payload.attempted: Reduce row-chunk size to expose finer-grained overlap.
payload.lesson: Chunking needs a scheduler/dataflow designed for chunks. It is not just a dependency knob.

established_fact.mechanism: Overlap granularity has a fixed cost. If the consumer GEMM is not chunk-aware, smaller chunks can multiply overhead faster than they expose overlap.

payload.observed: Finer chunks were much slower because each chunk repeats GEMM launch and scheduler overhead and reduces tile utilization.
payload.root_cause: Overlap granularity has a fixed cost. If the consumer GEMM is not chunk-aware, smaller chunks can multiply overhead faster than they expose overlap.
